highlights.content: [![The McGill International Review](https://mironline.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Website-logo-3.jpg) The McGill International Review - Canada's premier undergraduate journal of international affairs.](https://mironline.ca/) [![MIR](https://mironline.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Website-logo-3.jpg)](https://mironline.ca/) # China’s Bid To Win the AI Race [By **Ivy Luders**](https://mironline.ca/author/ivyluders/ "Browse Author Articles") ![]() **Share** In January 2025, Chinese startup DeepSeek shocked the artificial intelligence world by releasing a large language model (LLM) rivalling those of American tech giants. [Built](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html) with a fraction of the cost—reportedly around [10 times less](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html) than Meta’s latest technology at the time—and with far fewer and less advanced chips than its American counterparts, the novel model [caused](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/tech-stocks-react-chinas-deepseek-sparks-us-worries-ai-race-rcna189394) international financial markets to freefall as investors questioned the future of American AI dominance. The success of DeepSeek’s model [marks](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/28/technology/china-deepseek-ai-silicon-valley.html?eafs_enabled=false) a significant escalation in what has been dubbed an “AI arms race” between the United States and China. This AI race unfolds across many dimensions, beyond merely developing the most advanced LLM. Critically, the “winner” of the AI race will be determined by how deeply AI is integrated into each country’s domestic economy and, ultimately, into the global one.  In [comparing](https://www.capitalgroup.com/advisor/ca/en/insights/articles/united-states-versus-china-who-winning-ai-race.html) the US and China, the US has greater access to private capital, with private AI investment more than [23 times](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report/economy) that of China’s in 2025. The US also clings to a quickly shrinking lead in frontier AI, with its top model’s performance just [2.7 per cent](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report) ahead of China’s. Despite this, China’s AI development model may be more suitable for global diffusion because of its government-industry coordination, open-weight models, and growing partnerships abroad—particularly in the Global South. These strategies have [boosted](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/18681026261434029) inter-firm competition domestically and internationally, lowered costs, and accelerated innovation, thereby helping China consolidate its soft power internationally.  Moreover, US semiconductor export controls on China have further [incentivized](https://www.forbes.com/sites/craigsmith/2025/09/02/chinas-ai-self-sufficiency-push-is-challenging-us-dominance/) the country’s technological self-reliance while exposing the US’s dependence on Taiwan’s advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry. As the US’s lead in frontier AI ebbs, China may be better positioned to deploy its AI internationally, especially if the US does not stabilize relations with its allies, increase technological independence, and lower costs. This global shift would have major economic, security, political, and ideological implications as well as other unforeseen consequences. The Chinese government’s strategy for LLM dominance [emphasizes](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/18681026261434029) diffusion and competition domestically through a combination of state direction, local subsidies, and market forces. At the national level, Beijing has [implemented](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/18681026261434029) a strict regulatory framework and initiatives to [integrate](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/18681026261434029) AI across key sectors, including education, robotics, and intelligent vehicles. highlights.content: ![]() ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-light.svg) ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia tells data center partners to limit China exposure below 50%: report ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![Jensen Huang](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/invezz:e53c09b27094b-0d92e7daf13332cdb6119771fa1ebd69-resized.webp) Nvidia NVDA has instructed its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday, amid Washington's increasing efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips. The world's largest chipmaker has reportedly told cloud computing partners to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese companies. The guidance was communicated verbally through Nvidia's sales teams and regional offices rather than through formal written instructions, the report said. The reported restrictions apply to new contracts and do not affect existing agreements. Nvidia has not officially confirmed the policy. **What has Nvidia told its partners?** The reported requirement would push data center operators to diversify their customer base and reduce the proportion of computing services supplied to Chinese businesses. The development could create additional challenges for Chinese AI companies that have relied on overseas cloud providers to access advanced Nvidia processors. Renting computing capacity outside China has offered these companies an alternative route to using powerful American chips without importing them directly. A follow-up report by The Information said Nvidia's instructions were intended to encourage a broader customer mix and were not being enforced as a mandatory restriction. The distinction suggests the company is seeking greater oversight of how its chips are used. **Nvidia defends American chip infrastructure** America cannot win the AI race unless America's AI infrastructure wins worldwide -- if the world's clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well. Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report. However, the company emphasized the importance of expanding the global reach of American-built AI infrastructure. "Datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide," the company said in a statement cited by AFP. It added that America's ability to compete in AI depends on its infrastructure being widely adopted across global cloud networks. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told AFP that she was unaware of the reported restrictions. She added that Beijing hopes companies from all countries will receive a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment. **Nvidia under scanner** The reported move comes as Washington continues to restrict exports of advanced AI processors to China, citing national security concerns and the potential military applications of the technology. Last week, a New York Times investigation reported that US intelligence officials suspected a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed of passing commercial information to Beijing. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had reportedly developed a close relationship with the executive. Nvidia has said their interactions were routine business meetings. Separately, a contractor linked to server maker Super Micro pleaded guilty in October to participating in a scheme to illegally divert Nvidia-powered AI servers to China. Prosecutors allege that there are two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server ​maker, who conspired to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation ​of export laws. ## [NVDA chart](/chart/?symbol=NASDAQ%3ANVDA) ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Invezz](/news-flow/?provider=inve...

highlights.content: [Skip to content](#responsive-grid-main-content) [###### < ALL PRESS RELEASES](/en/news/press-releases/) # Snowflake Delivers the Foundation for Autonomous Data Engineering, Powering the Agentic Enterprise with Trusted, Live Data ![](/content/dam/snowflake-site/general/static/images/hero-dots.png) ![Snowflake](/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--0ae1bdf4-21ec-4b14-8eb3-f2d57dbabcab/expedition-data-engineering.png?quality=85&preferwebp=true) *With new Snowflake innovations, AI agents help keep data pipelines healthy and businesses get live data they can act on* * **The Blueprint for Self-Healing Pipelines, With Engineers in Control:** CoCo Cloud Agents and CoCo Automations take on recurring pipeline fixes, with engineers providing guidelines and guardrails * **From Reactive Reporting to Proactive Action:** Snowflake delivers end-to-end, real-time analytics capabilities to power dashboards, apps, and AI agents * **More Data, Ready for AI:** Teams can move Apache Spark™ workloads onto Snowflake with fewer code changes, so more data is governed and available to AI **SNOWFLAKE EXPEDITION 2026 – Nov. 3, 2026 –** [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/) (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today at [Snowflake Expedition 2026](https://www.snowflake.com/en/expedition/) announced new [autonomous data engineering](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/use-cases/autonomous-data-engineering/) and real-time analytics innovations that help enterprises build and run the trusted data foundation AI agents rely on. Autonomous data engineering puts AI agents to work on the recurring tasks of building, running, and fixing data pipelines, with engineers deciding what goes into production. With new capabilities in [Snowflake CoCo](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-coco/), the coding agent where you build faster, data teams can build autonomous workflows to tackle recurring, repetitive tasks like repairing pipelines. End-to-end, real-time analytics capabilities keep pipelines fed with live data from across the business, with governance controls applied from the moment it lands and everywhere it’s used. As companies hand more decisions to AI agents, the need for trusted data powering those agents matters more than ever. If an agent works with yesterday's numbers or with a pipeline that is broken, it will act on the wrong information. At the speed agents operate and the rate businesses are growing, those mistakes add up fast. Yet for many enterprises, that data still depends on hand-written pipelines and streaming systems pieced together from several tools. Data teams spend a lot of their time just keeping it all running. Snowflake's latest capabilities help enterprises scale AI with confidence. Agents act on live, governed data, decisions keep pace with the business, and data teams can take on more of what their organization actually needs. "Every AI success story has a data team behind it," said Christian Kleinerman, EVP of Product, Snowflake. "However, even as AI scales across the enterprise, those teams are still keeping data accurate largely by hand. With data volumes continuing to skyrocket and agents taking on more of the work, that approach won't hold. Snowflake is bringing autonomous agents into data engineering and real-time data onto one governed platform, so data teams can stop holding the foundation together and spend more time building on it." **Putting Agents to Work on Recurring Data Tasks, So Teams Can Focus on Business Outcomes** At the pace AI is scaling, data engineers can't afford to spend their days keeping pipelines running. Most data teams already use AI coding assistants, but those tools typically only speed up one engineer's work on one laptop, and they don't know how a company's data connects or which rules apply to it. The jump from its own prior model is enormous. On Terminal-Bench v2.1, a benchmark that tests an AI agent's ability to complete real command-line tasks, LongCat-2.5 scored 88.4, up from 70.8 for LongCat-2.0. On DeepSWE v1.1, a tougher agentic coding benchmark, it posted 64.6 against LongCat-2.0's 9.7. That's a nearly sevenfold gain in under three months. Meituan is China's largest food delivery company, the one that sends scooters weaving through Beijing traffic to drop off hot pot and bubble tea. It is also, somewhat quietly, building one of the more serious open-weight model labs in the country under its LongCat brand, run separately from the consumer app. LongCat-2.5 is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, of which only about 48 billion activate for any given task. It's the same scale as its predecessor but retrained for far longer task chains. It handles a million-token context window. It can also output up to 128,000 tokens in a single response, which matters for a model meant to work through an entire codebase rather than one function at a time. The model is natively multimodal, meaning it processes text and images through the same underlying token system instead of bolting a separate vision module on top. highlights.content: [![AIM](/assets/aim-logo-0ZnRqAR3.png)](/) [Subscribe](/subscribe) Article Complete [![AIM](/assets/aim-logo-0ZnRqAR3.png)](/) MIT Researchers Show LLMs Can Read and Edit Neural Network Weights Without Retraining ![MIT Researchers Show LLMs Can Read and Edit Neural Network Weights Without Retraining](/cdn-cgi/image/width=1600,quality=60,format=auto,fit=scale-down/https://zdpdvwhvukelzzbzbjvh.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/imported-images/1769001372847-19619404-6ae6-4f3f-8daa-84a92798a544-jg48vd.webp) [AI News](/ai-news) # MIT Researchers Show LLMs Can Read and Edit Neural Network Weights Without Retraining By modifying just 0.016% of the model’s weights, Astra increased its score on the MATH-500 benchmark from 7.9% to 48.1%. [Siddharth Jindal](/author/siddharth-jindal) Published Updated ## Key takeaways * MIT researchers demonstrated that large language models can read and edit neural network weights without traditional retraining methods. * The technique, called Weight-Space Programming, allows LLMs to modify weights based on natural-language instructions. * The experiment showcased that modifying a small percentage of weights significantly improved the performance of existing models. * Frontier LLMs like GPT-6 Astra excel at interpreting neural network weights beyond human or conventional algorithm capabilities. * The research indicates a potential shift in how neural networks can be optimised and improved efficiently. 5 min Follow[Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://analyticsindiamag.com)[Google News](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqMggKIixDQklTR3dnTWFoY0tGV0Z1WVd4NWRHbGpjMmx1WkdsaGJXRm5MbU52YlNnQVAB?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)[WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaCAfcMGehEGsj0COi2R)[Telegram](https://t.me/joinchat/TrPapX0NesB579PQ) Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) have shown that [large language models (LLMs)](https://analyticsindiamag.com/it-services/why-indias-it-giants-are-swapping-bloated-llms-for-small-language-models) can read, interpret, and modify neural network weights directly, without relying on traditional training methods like gradient descent. In a research [blog post](https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/) published on November 2, the researchers introduced a technique called Weight-Space Programming, which lets general-purpose LLMs examine a neural network’s weights, identify problems in its behaviour, and modify them based on natural-language instructions. The research was conducted by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab, all affiliated with MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL). The researchers used OpenAI’s [GPT-6 Astra](https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/anthropic-weighs-new-ai-model-as-openais-gpt-6-astra-gains-ground) to demonstrate the approach across eight experiments, including identifying what a neural network was trained to do, writing networks from scratch and improving the mathematical reasoning capabilities of an existing language model. “We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we'd expect from humans or conventional algorithms,” the researchers wrote. One key experiment involved improving Qwen3.5-0.8B, a small language model, without retraining it or using gradient information. Astra identified a problem in the model’s weights that caused it to repeat reasoning steps instead of producing answers. By modifying just 0.016% of the model’s weights, Astra increased its score on the MATH-500 benchmark from 7.9% to 48.1%. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [Subscribe Now](https://www.pressreader.com/philippines/daily-tribune-philippines "E-paper / digital newspaper via PressReader")[Support Us](/support "Support the newsroom") [TECHTALKS](/techtalks) * [iProov biometric AI security](/topic/iproov-biometric-ai-security) * [Human Approval and Presence Specification](/topic/human-approval-and-presence-specification) * [AI agent human approval system](/topic/ai-agent-human-approval-system) # iProov brings biometric safeguards to autonomous systems DT··2 MIN READ ![BIOMETRIC authentication company iProov has introduced a security service requiring verified human approval for sensitive actions performed by autonomous AI agents.](https://images.assettype.com/tribune/2026-11-03/n791jhzq/iProov.jpg?w=720&auto=format&q=55&rect=0%2C8%2C1366%2C768&h=405&fit=crop) BIOMETRIC authentication company iProov has introduced a security service requiring verified human approval for sensitive actions performed by autonomous AI agents. Photograph courtesy of iProov Text size Save Biometric authentication company iProov has launched a security service designed to prevent autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents from carrying out sensitive actions without verified human approval. Announced on 2 November 2026, the service uses facial verification and cryptographic authentication to confirm that an authorized person has approved a specific action before an AI agent can execute it. The technology implements the Human Approval and Presence Specification (HAPS), introduced in September 2026, and integrates with open-source AI infrastructure platform agentgateway and authorization management provider Cerbos. Under the system, an AI agent attempting a high-risk transaction, such as transferring funds, can be required to obtain human authorization. The designated approver reviews the proposed action and completes a biometric presence check. If approved, the system issues a digitally signed, single-use credential tied to the transaction. Any changes to the transaction details, including the payment amount or recipient, invalidate the approval. iProov said the technology provides an auditable record of authorization while helping prevent AI agents from impersonating human decision-makers. “For organizations to realize the full potential of agentic AI, they need to task agents with increasingly consequential responsibilities. But some actions must remain subject to human control, approval and accountability,” said iProov founder and CEO Andrew Bud. Cerbos will determine when human approval is required, while iProov verifies the approver’s identity and presence. The launch comes as businesses increasingly deploy AI agents capable of independently executing tasks, raising concerns about unauthorized transactions, accountability and security. The HAPS specification is open source, allowing other technology providers to develop compatible approval systems. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [Subscribe Now](https://www.pressreader.com/philippines/daily-tribune-philippines "E-paper / digital newspaper via PressReader")[Support Us](/support "Support the newsroom") [TECHTALKS](/techtalks) * [iProov biometric AI security](/topic/iproov-biometric-ai-security) * [Human Approval and Presence Specification](/topic/human-approval-and-presence-specification) * [AI agent human approval system](/topic/ai-agent-human-approval-system) # iProov brings biometric safeguards to autonomous systems DT··2 MIN READ ![BIOMETRIC authentication company iProov has introduced a security service requiring verified human approval for sensitive actions performed by autonomous AI agents.](https://images.assettype.com/tribune/2026-11-03/n791jhzq/iProov.jpg?w=720&auto=format&q=55&rect=0%2C8%2C1366%2C768&h=405&fit=crop) BIOMETRIC authentication company iProov has introduced a security service requiring verified human approval for sensitive actions performed by autonomous AI agents. Photograph courtesy of iProov Text size Save Biometric authentication company iProov has launched a security service designed to prevent autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents from carrying out sensitive actions without verified human approval. Announced on 2 November 2026, the service uses facial verification and cryptographic authentication to confirm that an authorized person has approved a specific action before an AI agent can execute it. The technology implements the Human Approval and Presence Specification (HAPS), introduced in September 2026, and integrates with open-source AI infrastructure platform agentgateway and authorization management provider Cerbos. Under the system, an AI agent attempting a high-risk transaction, such as transferring funds, can be required to obtain human authorization. The designated approver reviews the proposed action and completes a biometric presence check. If approved, the system issues a digitally signed, single-use credential tied to the transaction. Any changes to the transaction details, including the payment amount or recipient, invalidate the approval. iProov said the technology provides an auditable record of authorization while helping prevent AI agents from impersonating human decision-makers. “For organizations to realize the full potential of agentic AI, they need to task agents with increasingly consequential responsibilities. But some actions must remain subject to human control, approval and accountability,” said iProov founder and CEO Andrew Bud. Cerbos will determine when human approval is required, while iProov verifies the approver’s identity and presence. The launch comes as businesses increasingly deploy AI agents capable of independently executing tasks, raising concerns about unauthorized transactions, accountability and security. The HAPS specification is open source, allowing other technology providers to develop compatible approval systems. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#responsive-grid-main-content) [###### < ALL PRESS RELEASES](/en/news/press-releases/) # Snowflake CoCo and CoWork Power the Agentic Enterprise, Grounded in Governed Data and Built for Autonomous Action ![](/content/dam/snowflake-site/general/static/images/hero-dots.png) ![Snowflake](/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--6b8beab8-08b2-41ff-82b4-15bf61e1896a/expedition-d1-pr-coco-cowork-bots-1000x428.png?quality=85&preferwebp=true) *Snowflake CoCo and CoWork Bots work in the background, act directly in the tools teams already use, and check in only when a decision or sign-off is required* ![Snowflake](/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--c26706e7-d2ec-4ce5-b83f-bf32097f6a3f/expedition-d1-pr-cowork-1000x428-r02-%25281%2529.png?quality=85&preferwebp=true) *Snowflake CoCo and CoWork reimagine how enterprises work with AI, bringing together personal agents, role-aware intelligence, and automations* * **An Entirely New Class of Agents:** Always-on CoCo and CoWork Bots work proactively in the background, bringing in users only when work is ready or a human decision is needed * **More Automation, Wherever Teams Work:** Automations in CoCo and CoWork handle recurring work on their own, and plug seamlessly into Slack, Excel, mobile, and existing workflows * **Personalized Insights Improve Over Time**: Shared skills, Memory, and Artifacts like dashboards and reports allow teams to build on each other’s work, and the agents get better with every run **SNOWFLAKE EXPEDITION 2026** **– Nov. 3, 2026 –** [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/) (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today at [Snowflake Expedition 2026](https://www.snowflake.com/en/expedition/) announced new innovations that bridge the gap between what enterprises ask AI agents to do, and what those agents act on and understand about the business. The result is agents they can rely on to do real work, not just answer questions. This marks a fundamental evolution in enterprise intelligence, moving organizations from software that waits for a prompt to an autonomous layer driving continuous execution. Significant updates to [Snowflake CoCo](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-coco/), the coding agent for data teams, and [Snowflake CoWork](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-cowork/), the personal work agent for knowledge workers, help the agents better understand how each business runs, let them take on recurring work on their own, and help them improve with each request. Pushing autonomous work even further, new **CoCo and CoWork Bots**5 serve as always-on AI coworkers that continuously work in the background, act directly in the tools teams already use, and check in only when a decision or sign-off is required. The agentic enterprise is changing how work gets done, with agents saving teams hours on everyday tasks and accelerating longer-term projects. It also demands a new standard of trust. An agent that doesn't know how a company defines revenue, or the rules it runs on, may give a confident wrong answer that someone has to catch. To earn that trust, agents must understand how the business uniquely operates, and work within uncompromising built-in governance. Snowflake's new innovations give CoCo and CoWork that understanding from the start, enabling agents to act autonomously across business workflows, freeing teams to put their energy into the creative, forward-looking work only people can do. For over 14,500 global enterprises, Snowflake already sits at the center of the data, business context, AI models, and workflows that agents depend on, serving as the governed control plane for the agentic enterprise. CoWork is now used by more than 5,800 accounts and CoCo by more than 9,1001, with organizations such as **Cisco, Docusign**, **Klarent, Pacific Life Insurance Company**, **Shelter Mutual Insurance Company**, and **United Rentals** putting both to work across their business. [Apple](https://www.apple.com) just became the first major tech company to formally warn investors about the risks of AI agents going rogue. Buried in the company's annual regulatory filing is a stark admission - the autonomous AI systems everyone's racing to deploy could exceed their permissions, resist instructions, or take actions that are difficult to reverse. LLMs.content: [![The McGill International Review](https://mironline.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Website-logo-3.jpg) The McGill International Review - Canada's premier undergraduate journal of international affairs.](https://mironline.ca/) [![MIR](https://mironline.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Website-logo-3.jpg)](https://mironline.ca/) # China’s Bid To Win the AI Race [By **Ivy Luders**](https://mironline.ca/author/ivyluders/ "Browse Author Articles") ![]() **Share** In January 2025, Chinese startup DeepSeek shocked the artificial intelligence world by releasing a large language model (LLM) rivalling those of American tech giants. [Built](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html) with a fraction of the cost—reportedly around [10 times less](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html) than Meta’s latest technology at the time—and with far fewer and less advanced chips than its American counterparts, the novel model [caused](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/tech-stocks-react-chinas-deepseek-sparks-us-worries-ai-race-rcna189394) international financial markets to freefall as investors questioned the future of American AI dominance. The success of DeepSeek’s model [marks](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/28/technology/china-deepseek-ai-silicon-valley.html?eafs_enabled=false) a significant escalation in what has been dubbed an “AI arms race” between the United States and China. This AI race unfolds across many dimensions, beyond merely developing the most advanced LLM. Critically, the “winner” of the AI race will be determined by how deeply AI is integrated into each country’s domestic economy and, ultimately, into the global one.  In [comparing](https://www.capitalgroup.com/advisor/ca/en/insights/articles/united-states-versus-china-who-winning-ai-race.html) the US and China, the US has greater access to private capital, with private AI investment more than [23 times](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report/economy) that of China’s in 2025. The US also clings to a quickly shrinking lead in frontier AI, with its top model’s performance just [2.7 per cent](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report) ahead of China’s. Despite this, China’s AI development model may be more suitable for global diffusion because of its government-industry coordination, open-weight models, and growing partnerships abroad—particularly in the Global South. [Siddharth Jindal](/author/siddharth-jindal) Published Updated ## Key takeaways * MIT researchers demonstrated that large language models can read and edit neural network weights without traditional retraining methods. * The technique, called Weight-Space Programming, allows LLMs to modify weights based on natural-language instructions. * The experiment showcased that modifying a small percentage of weights significantly improved the performance of existing models. * Frontier LLMs like GPT-6 Astra excel at interpreting neural network weights beyond human or conventional algorithm capabilities. * The research indicates a potential shift in how neural networks can be optimised and improved efficiently. 5 min Follow[Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://analyticsindiamag.com)[Google News](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqMggKIixDQklTR3dnTWFoY0tGV0Z1WVd4NWRHbGpjMmx1WkdsaGJXRm5MbU52YlNnQVAB?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)[WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaCAfcMGehEGsj0COi2R)[Telegram](https://t.me/joinchat/TrPapX0NesB579PQ) Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) have shown that [large language models (LLMs)](https://analyticsindiamag.com/it-services/why-indias-it-giants-are-swapping-bloated-llms-for-small-language-models) can read, interpret, and modify neural network weights directly, without relying on traditional training methods like gradient descent. The research was conducted by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab, all affiliated with MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL). One key experiment involved improving Qwen3.5-0.8B, a small language model, without retraining it or using gradient information. Astra identified a problem in the model’s weights that caused it to repeat reasoning steps instead of producing answers. By modifying just 0.016% of the model’s weights, Astra increased its score on the MATH-500 benchmark from 7.9% to 48.1%. Its score on GSM8K, another mathematical reasoning benchmark, increased from 13.8% to 67.1%. The researchers also found that the changes improved the model’s instruction-following performance. Its IFEval score increased from 21% to 62.3%. In the first set of experiments, the researchers tested whether Astra could identify a network’s behaviour ...

8 LLM Inference Frameworks You Should Try in 2026 Compare LLM inference frameworks for production serving, request batching, KV cache management, and efficient deployment. By **[Bala Priya C](https://www.kdnuggets.com/author/bala-priya)**, KDnuggets Contributing Editor & Technical Content Specialist on November 3, 2026 in [Language Models](https://www.kdnuggets.com/tag/language-models) --- A model that runs in a notebook serves one request at a time. A production endpoint receives many requests at once, and each one needs GPU memory for its **[key-value (KV) cache](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/coding-the-kv-cache-in-llms)**, a slot in the batch, and a response stream. Plain **[PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/)** or **[Hugging Face Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/index)** can serve the model, but you have to build the request scheduling, cache management, and API layer around it yourself. Inference frameworks supply those pieces. They sit between the model and your application and cover token generation, KV cache management, request batching, and the API surface, so you don't build that machinery for every model you ship. With a suitable framework, the same GPU can serve more concurrent requests at lower latency with no change to the model. This article covers inference frameworks for high-throughput, data-center-scale serving, as well as tools designed for local, edge, and low-resource environments. Customers will expect an assistant to understand their needs, act securely on enterprise systems, and involve a human when necessary. > > — Ritesh Patil, Founder and Chief Delivery Officer at Mobisoft Infotech HOUSTON, TX, UNITED STATES, November 3, 2026 /[EINPresswire.com](https://www.einpresswire.com/)/ — Mobisoft Infotech, an [AI-native product engineering company](https://mobisoftinfotech.com/services/digital-product-engineering), today announced expanded Agentic Conversational AI solutions. These solutions help enterprises build intelligent digital agents that can do more than answer customer questions. Unlike traditional chatbots, agentic systems do more than provide scripted responses or retrieve information. They can understand user intent and access authorized enterprise data. They can also use business applications and APIs. They execute multi-step tasks and coordinate workflows across systems. Mobisoft’s approach combines conversational AI, [generative AI](https://mobisoftinfotech.com/services/generative-ai), enterprise knowledge systems, AI agents, workflow orchestration, and systems integration. This helps organizations create AI-powered experiences. These experiences can move a customer interaction from conversation to resolution. For example, instead of simply telling a customer how to reschedule an appointment, an AI agent can authenticate the customer and check available slots. It can then update the scheduling system and confirm the new appointment. It can also trigger the appropriate follow-up communication. Similarly, an enterprise conversational AI agent could help a customer check an order or modify a service request. It could also initiate a claim, update account information, or retrieve personalized information. It could create a support ticket too. When needed, it could escalate an exception to a human employee. Moving From Conversational AI to Action-Oriented AI: Many enterprises have already deployed chatbots and conversational interfaces. However, these systems frequently remain disconnected from the applications and workflows required to actually complete a customer request. Mobisoft’s conversational [AI agent development](https://mobisoftinfotech.com/services/ai-agent-development-company) approach is designed to bridge that gap. The solutions can be engineered to support capabilities including: – Secure user authentication and identity-aware interactions – Retrieval of information from enterprise knowledge bases and business systems – Personalized responses based on customer context and permissions – Integration with CRM, ERP, scheduling, ticketing, payment, and other enterprise applications – Appointment booking and rescheduling – Creation and modification of service requests – Workflow initiation and task execution – Intelligent routing and human escalation – Multi-step conversational workflows – Voice and text-based conversational experiences – Multilingual interactions – Auditability, guardrails, monitoring, and human-in-the-loop controls Organizations can combine AI agents with enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, business rules, and workflow orchestration. This creates conversational systems that explain what a customer should do next. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The acquisition adds 3CLogic’s cloud-based voice engagement platform to PartnerOne’s software portfolio as businesses increasingly adopt AI-powered tools to automate customer service operations and connect interactions with existing enterprise systems. 3CLogic combines conversational AI, intelligent automation and cloud contact center capabilities with its proprietary Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) infrastructure. Its technology integrates voice interactions with enterprise customer relationship management (CRM), IT service management (ITSM) and other business platforms, allowing organizations to automate routine requests while supporting human agents handling more complex customer interactions. The platform is designed to operate alongside existing enterprise applications rather than replace them, enabling companies to add AI voice agents, intelligent call routing and automated workflows to their current technology environments. “3CLogic brings together important capabilities in enterprise software, voice AI, and workflow automation in a market with significant opportunity for growth,” said **Suzanne Fortman**, Vice President at PartnerOne. “At PartnerOne, we acquire software companies with the intent of investing in their potential and helping them become better and stronger over the long term.” The acquisition is intended to provide 3CLogic with additional resources to expand its technology platform, strengthen customer relationships and accelerate product development in enterprise voice AI. 3CLogic’s offerings include AI-powered self-service, generative AI, conversational AI, agent automation and coaching, and sentiment analytics. These capabilities are designed to help organizations reduce manual customer service tasks, improve agent productivity and connect customer interactions with the business processes needed to resolve requests. The transaction also expands PartnerOne’s exposure to enterprise AI applications as organizations move beyond experimental deployments toward automation integrated with operational workflows. “Joining PartnerOne creates an exciting opportunity for 3CLogic to build on the technology, customer relationships, and market presence we’ve developed,” said Denis Seynhaeve, Chairman and CEO of 3CLogic. “PartnerOne’s long-term ownership approach aligns with our commitment to helping customers improve service experiences and advance their automation initiatives.” PartnerOne acquires and operates enterprise software companies, focusing on long-term ownership, operational improvements and continued investment in product development and market expansion. The company reports that its software businesses serve more than 2,000 enterprise and government organizations, including 80% of the world’s largest companies. AI Product.content: SecurityBrief Australia - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers [![SecurityBrief Australia logo](/brands/sb-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com.au) ![ThreatLocker launches control for corporate AI agents](https://securitybrief.com.au/uploads/story/2026/11/04/blocked-ai-agent-enterprise-security-control-panel-data-center-story-323323.webp) [AI Security](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/ai-security) [Zero Trust Security](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/zero-trust-security) [AI](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/artificial-intelligence) # ThreatLocker launches control for corporate AI agents Wed, 4th Nov 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://securitybrief.com.au/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) ThreatLocker has launched Zero Trust AI Control, a tool designed to manage what AI agents can do inside corporate systems. The product is aimed at organisations deploying agentic AI across their environments. The tool applies external controls to AI agents, allowing security teams to decide which systems, applications and services an agent may access. Those limits remain in place even when an agent calls on other software, scripts or browser-based services to complete a task. The launch comes as businesses give AI tools a more active role in day-to-day operations, moving beyond information retrieval to taking actions inside business systems. That shift has created a security issue because many existing safeguards still rely on the AI system following its own rules. Zero Trust AI Control uses a default-deny model, allowing an AI agent to reach only the resources needed for a defined job while blocking access to everything else. The controls sit outside the AI deployment itself, helping maintain boundaries if an agent behaves unexpectedly. According to ThreatLocker, security teams can begin with pre-built policies and then adjust them to suit their own environment. The product is designed to reduce the amount of manual work involved in setting limits around AI activity. In current enterprise use, a single request to an AI agent can set off a chain of actions across multiple parts of an IT estate. ThreatLocker says its new tool is built to govern that workflow from start to finish by controlling what agents can access, execute and connect to as they move between applications and services. **Broader controls** ThreatLocker positioned the product as part of a wider set of controls around AI use. Used alongside ThreatLocker Allowlisting and Web Content Control, the new tool is intended to let security teams decide both which AI applications are permitted into an environment and what approved agents may do once active. That approach reflects a wider debate in cybersecurity over how to contain software that acts with increasing autonomy. AI agents can carry out tasks by interacting with browsers, internal tools and external services, making access management more complex than traditional user-based permissions. ThreatLocker, which focuses on zero trust cybersecurity products, says it serves more than 70,000 organisations worldwide. The business is headquartered in Orlando, Florida, and also has offices in Dublin, Dubai and Brisbane. Danny Jenkins, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of ThreatLocker, set out the company's view in comments accompanying the launch. The system aims to enable "verifiable inference," which can effectively prevent service providers from secretly replacing models in commercial operations (such as passing off a low-cost model as a high-performance model, or using a cheap model to exaggerate performance results). It can also be used to verify third-party claims about the execution of complex tasks. In terms of technical implementation, FlashProve requires AI labs to generate and publish specific "fingerprints" for the models they release, so that clients can perform cryptographic matching. The system's core advantage is that its fingerprinting mechanism does not reveal the model's internal weight data, balancing the confidentiality needs of commercial models with compatibility. In addition, this lightweight system supports verification directly on local devices. Currently, Anthropic has open-sourced the project's detailed technical specifications and working code on GitHub. At this stage, the research is mainly intended for sharing milestone results and industry reference, with no specific commercial deployment plans for now. Open Source AI.titleZh: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models' identity | TechCrunch
Open Source AI.content: Anthropic is working on an open-source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” – a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using. Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results. FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?” To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device. As part of the announcement, researchers released a detailed technical specification and working code for various elements of the system, which is publicly available under an open-source license on GitHub. Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab. “This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda,” researchers explain in the announcement post. “We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.” Topics When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. Infra & Chips.content: ![]() ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-light.svg) ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia tells data center partners to limit China exposure below 50%: report ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![Jensen Huang](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/invezz:e53c09b27094b-0d92e7daf13332cdb6119771fa1ebd69-resized.webp) Nvidia NVDA has instructed its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday, amid Washington's increasing efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips. The world's largest chipmaker has reportedly told cloud computing partners to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese companies. The guidance was communicated verbally through Nvidia's sales teams and regional offices rather than through formal written instructions, the report said. The reported restrictions apply to new contracts and do not affect existing agreements. Nvidia has not officially confirmed the policy. **What has Nvidia told its partners?** The reported requirement would push data center operators to diversify their customer base and reduce the proportion of computing services supplied to Chinese businesses. The development could create additional challenges for Chinese AI companies that have relied on overseas cloud providers to access advanced Nvidia processors. Renting computing capacity outside China has offered these companies an alternative route to using powerful American chips without importing them directly. A follow-up report by The Information said Nvidia's instructions were intended to encourage a broader customer mix and were not being enforced as a mandatory restriction. The distinction suggests the company is seeking greater oversight of how its chips are used. **Nvidia defends American chip infrastructure** America cannot win the AI race unless America's AI infrastructure wins worldwide -- if the world's clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well. Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report. However, the company emphasized the importance of expanding the global reach of American-built AI infrastructure. "Datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide," the company said in a statement cited by AFP. It added that America's ability to compete in AI depends on its infrastructure being widely adopted across global cloud networks. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told AFP that she was unaware of the reported restrictions. She added that Beijing hopes companies from all countries will receive a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment. **Nvidia under scanner** The reported move comes as Washington continues to restrict exports of advanced AI processors to China, citing national security concerns and the potential military applications of the technology. Last week, a New York Times investigation reported that US intelligence officials suspected a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed of passing commercial information to Beijing. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had reportedly developed a close relationship with the executive. Nvidia has said their interactions were routine business meetings. Separately, a contractor linked to server maker Super Micro pleaded guilty in October to participating in a scheme to illegally divert Nvidia-powered AI servers to China. Prosecutors allege that there are two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server ​maker, who conspired to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation ​of export laws. ## [NVDA chart](/chart/?symbol=NASDAQ%3ANVDA) ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Invezz](/news-flow/?provider=inve...

Press Release Binding order of over €60 million[1]: 2CRSi to deliver 83 NVIDIA HGX B300 AI servers to Exaion by the end of 2026 Exaion builds on its strategic partnership with 2CRSi, in place since 2021, to accelerate the development of sovereign AI inference Strasbourg, France – November 3, 2026 – 2CRSi (ISIN: FR0013341781), a designer and manufacturer of high-performance, energy-efficient servers, announces that it has received a binding order of over €60 million from Exaion, its partner since 2021, for 83 NVIDIA HGX B300 AI servers, along with associated storage and maintenance services. 2CRSi and Exaion: a strategic partnership since 2021 supporting sustainable digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence Since 2021, 2CRSi and Exaion have been building a strategic collaboration to design and deploy high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure that combines computing power, energy efficiency, and a low environmental footprint. The partnership draws on the complementary expertise of the two companies. 2CRSi contributes its know-how in designing and manufacturing high-performance servers, along with its innovative immersion cooling technologies, while Exaion brings its expertise in digital infrastructure, cloud, and advanced computing services. Exaion currently operates four data centers in France and Canada and aims to reach 300 MW of capacity, with 20 MW expected to be operational in 2027. This new order will enable 2CRSi to support its customer as it expands its offering from model training to private on-premises inference, supporting data control and digital sovereignty. Fatih BALYELI, Chairman and CEO of Exaion, said: “The arrival of these servers will allow us to significantly accelerate the rollout of our strategy. Private on-premises inference is a key priority for companies that want to take full advantage of artificial intelligence while keeping control of their strategic data. At Exaion, we firmly believe that digital sovereignty depends on the ability to deploy high-performing, secure, and fully controlled computing infrastructure. Our partnership with 2CRSi brings together complementary technological expertise to support this ambition and meet organizations’ growing needs for trusted AI.” This collaboration illustrates 2CRSi’s position as a leading technology player in next-generation computing infrastructure, at the crossroads of artificial intelligence, energy efficiency, and digital transformation. It also demonstrates the company’s ability to support specialized operators in deploying HPC and AI solutions, in France and internationally. The 83 servers will be deployed by the end of 2026: the first 17 will be delivered this week, 33 by the end of November, and the final 33 before the end of December. Alain WILMOUTH, Chairman and CEO of 2CRSi, said: “We are very proud to strengthen our long-standing partnership with Exaion. This new order reflects the renewed confidence of our customers and suppliers in our solutions. [DATA & AI](/data-and-ai) # E2E Networks plans 5.4 MW Blackwell expansion, launches Blaze AI inference service ## E2E Networks plans to expand its AI infrastructure to 14.6 MW and has launched Blaze, a pay-per-token inference service for open AI models. Announced on October 26, 2026, the expansion will comprise NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other GPUs. ![author-image](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/100x0/filters:format(webp)/dq/media/member_avatars/2026/04/30/2026-04-30t115507243z-preeti-2026-04-30-17-25-07.png ) [Preeti Anand](/author/preeti-anand) [![](/static/images/google_news.png) Follow Us](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqJQgKIh9DQklTRVFnTWFnMEtDMlJ4YVc1a2FXRXVZMjl0S0FBUAE?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen) New Update Listen to this article 0.75x1x1.5x 00:00/ 00:00 India's AI ecosystem is moving from experimental pilots towards production deployments, with domestic businesses, AI-native startups, research institutions, and public-sector organisations increasing their demand for training and inference infrastructure. Advertisment [Add DQIndia Info As A Trusted Source ![DQIndia Logo](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/580x326/filters:format(webp)/dq/media/media_files/2026/10/23/google-preferred-2026-10-23-15-14-28.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=dqindia.com) This shift is creating demand for high-performance graphics processing unit (GPU) infrastructure hosted in India, particularly among organisations managing sensitive data and large-scale AI workloads. Indian cloud provider E2E Networks has announced plans to expand its AI infrastructure capacity by approximately 5.4 megawatts (MW), alongside the launch of Blaze, a pay-per-token AI inference service. The proposed expansion would increase the company's existing capacity of approximately 9.2 MW to 14.6 MW, representing growth of nearly 59%. Advertisment Announced on October 26, 2026, the expansion will comprise NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other GPUs based on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture.
